name: Yang Two-Cone Decomposition and Gluing Dichotomy
statement: For an ample family $H$ in an active coordinate $e$, let $B_0,B_1$ be its sections, $A=B_0\cap B_1$ its full reduction, and $C=B_0\cup B_1$ its contraction. All four families are ample, and the Yang complex is the union of the cones $v_{e,0}*\Delta_{B_0}$ and $v_{e,1}*\Delta_{B_1}$ glued along $\Delta_A$. If $A$ and the opposite section are dismantlable ample and one section has an $A$-relative ample chain, then $H$ is dismantlable ample. Hence every active coordinate of an ample forbidden pc-minor has either a nonpeelable inherited site $A$, or a peelable site for which neither side is relatively shellable over $A$; in the latter case all three absolute Yang complexes are shellable.
proof: Facets on the two sides have distinct apex literals, and their intersection is the Yang complex of the section intersection. A relative ample chain deletes the exclusive concepts on one side as corners until only a peripheral expansion with base the opposite section and site A remains; the exact peripheral-expansion test peels it. In a forbidden pc-minor both sections and the contraction are positive proper minors, so if A is also positive, either relative shelling would contradict forbiddenness.
